leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Could / Couldn't
leadIn.content: Looking back at past abilities: When Tom was five years old, he could ride a bicycle, but he couldn't swim.

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Could / Couldn't?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Could / Couldn't require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Could / Couldn't
form.content: Subject + could / couldn't + base verb (past ability). Polite request: Could you + base verb?

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Could / Couldn't
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Could / Couldn't.

controlledPractice.question: 'I ___ swim when I was five.' (past ability)
controlledPractice.explanation: Could expresses ability in the past.

controlledPractice.question: Which is more polite?
controlledPractice.explanation: Could softens the request, sounding more polite.

controlledPractice.question: Fix: 'Could you to help me?'
controlledPractice.explanation: Like can, could never takes 'to' before the base verb.
